I was at 20-30 miles per week and went down very quickly to less than 5 around Christmas/New Year's this year. For about 2 months I'd still get the itch to run and put in some runs including a few 10k runs but the pain always became unbearable a few hours later. In February, I finally decided to rehab for a couple of months and refrain from running, hopeful that the injury would subside with typical RICE strategy. Didn't help.

Due to travel, work and more travel I wasn't able to get to a doctor until June. The diagnosis was insertional achilies tendinitis with calcification of the tendon and aggravated bursa due to Haglund's deformity. The doctor prescribed some physiotherapy and I was skeptical at first but man I feel like a million bucks. My achilies tendon and calf muscles were apparently so tight that you could play a tune on them.

As a mid-foot/toe runner my entire life, the excessive loading on the achilies explains the Haglund's growth. I don't plan to change my minimalist tendencies but the clear message I've learned was to stretch more, roll out the calf muscles and be more aware of the maintenance necessary to keep the insertion healthy. So learn from my lessons /v/running goats!
